Q: Thank you for taking the time to give this recorded statement. Can you confirm you're the driver of the vehicle
involved in the parking lot incident in Houston?
A: Yes, that's right. I was driving my own car.
Q: Can you describe where you were and what was happening when the collision occurred?
A: I was pulling into a space near the store entrance. It was a busy afternoon and the lot was pretty full. Another car
was backing out of a space a few rows over, and I didn't see it coming until it was already close.
Q: How fast were you traveling when you made contact?
A: Slowly, maybe walking pace. I'd just turned the wheel to line up with the space.
Q: Did the other driver say anything at the scene?
A: They apologized and said they didn't check their mirror. They gave me their insurance information, and we
exchanged details.
Q: Were there any passengers in your vehicle?
A: No, I was alone.
Q: Can you tell me about the injury you reported?
A: My right knee hit the steering column when the impact happened. It swelled up pretty quickly, and by that evening I
could barely bend it. I went to an urgent care clinic the next day, and they took X-rays and told me to follow up with an
orthopedist.
Q: Have you received any treatment since then?
A: I've had two physical therapy sessions so far and I'm scheduled for more. I'm still using a brace when I walk for
longer distances.
Q: Did you have any prior problems with that knee?
A: I had some minor soreness a few years ago after running, but nothing that stopped me from working or exercising.
It hadn't bothered me in a long time before this.
Q: Is there anything you'd like to add to your statement?
A: No, I think that covers it. I'm just hoping to get my car repaired and my knee back to normal.
Q: Thank you. This concludes the recorded statement.
</page>
